standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter valuative criterion of properness, in the form producing a morphism from the spectrum of a valuation ring compatible with a given morphism from its fraction field
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the morphism on the spectrum of the local ring at the point, which is the candidate germ of the extension.

standard_prerequisites.name: The lemma producing an open neighbourhood and a morphism with prescribed germ, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Spreads the germ at the point out to an actual morphism on a neighbourhood.

standard_prerequisites.name: The equalizer of two morphisms to a separated scheme over the base is a closed subscheme, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the two morphisms agree on a closed subscheme of the overlap, which contains the generic point.

standard_prerequisites.name: For every prime of a scheme there is an affine open containing it with the property that the ring of global functions injects into the local ring at that prime, cited from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof assume the source affine and integral with the local ring at the point a valuation ring whose fraction field is the residue field of the generic point.

core_obligations: Reduce the source: replacing the source by an open neighbourhood of the point is harmless, and by the cited affine-open statement one may assume the source affine with the ring of global functions contained in the local ring at the point, so that the source is integral and its generic point has residue field the fraction field of that valuation ring (proof lines 10426-10434).

Use properness: since the point lies in the closure of the given open and the open is therefore nonempty, it contains the generic point, so the valuative criterion of properness provides a morphism from the spectrum of the local ring to the target compatible with the given morphism on the open (proof lines 10435-10446).

Spread out the germ: apply the neighbourhood statement to the germ of that morphism at the point to obtain an open neighbourhood of the point and a morphism on it over the base whose germ at the point agrees with the valuative criterion's morphism (proof lines 10447-10453).

Glue: because the target is separated over the base, the equalizer of the two morphisms on the intersection of the two open sets is a closed subscheme; by construction both restrict to the same morphism from the generic point of that integral intersection, so the closed subscheme contains the generic point and hence is everything, and the two morphisms glue on the union of the two opens (proof lines 10454-10473).
proof_roadmap: Make the source affine and integral with the local ring at the point a valuation ring, so that the generic point realizes its fraction field (proof lines 10426-10434).

Get a morphism on the spectrum of that valuation ring from properness, spread its germ to a neighbourhood, and glue it with the given morphism using separatedness of the target (proof lines 10435-10473).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a morphism from an open subscheme into a proper scheme over the base extends over an open neighbourhood of a point lying in the closure of the open, provided the local ring at that point is a valuation ring and the source is reduced with finitely many components or Noetherian (statement lines 10424-10438). The counted proof has three distinct moves: it reduces the source to an affine integral one whose generic point realizes the fraction field of the valuation ring, applies the valuative criterion of properness to get a morphism on the spectrum of that local ring, spreads its germ to a neighbourhood, and glues it with the original morphism by comparing on the overlap through the equalizer, which is closed because the target is separated and contains the generic point (proof lines 10426-10473). It is H2: the argument is short but genuinely uses the valuative criterion and separatedness, and it is carried out entirely in the counted span.
